subject: Linguistics
title: Word Order Change
description: A quick, practical guide to Word Order Change.

hook.text: Old English was SOV—'The king the dragon slew.' Modern English is SVO—'The king slew the dragon.'

buildup.text: Word order can shift over centuries as case systems weaken and speakers need new clarity cues.

discovery.text: The most common orders worldwide are SOV and SVO—together they cover about 90% of languages.

twist.text: Word order changes are usually slow and incomplete—remnants of old orders survive in fixed phrases.

climax.text: 'Whom did you see?' preserves Old English object-first order in modern questions.

punchline.text: Even word order has a history—one buried in plain sight.

quiz.question: What was Old English's dominant word order?
